problems.title: Intersection of two straight lines
problems.question: Solve3x−1=−x+7 graphically.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: Plot y=3x−1 through(0,−1),(1,2), and y=−x+7 through(0,7),(1,6).
steps: Their intersection satisfies4x=8, so it is(2,5). The solution is the intersection’s x-coordinate,2.

problems.title: Eliminate a variable
problems.question: Solve2x+3y=8,3x−4y=−5.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
steps: Adding gives 17x=17, x=1. Substitute into2x+3y=8 to get y=2.

problems.title: Range after a shift and absolute value
problems.question: f has range[−7,7]. Find the range of|f(x)−3|.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
steps: This interval contains0, and its greatest magnitude is 10. Taking absolute values gives every value from 0 to 10.

problems.title: A perpendicular line through a reflected point
problems.question: A=(1,−1), B=(4,11). Find the line perpendicular to AB through B’s reflection in the y-axis.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: Slope AB=(11+1)/(4−1)=4. A perpendicular slope is −1/4; the reflected point is(−4,11).
steps: Point-slope for m gives y−11=−(x+4)/4, or y=−x/4+10.

problems.title: Horizontal levels of a piecewise graph
problems.question: f(x)=(x+5)/2 for x≤1, and −3x+4 for x>1. Give two a-values for which f(x)=a has one root.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: The first branch is one-to-one with range(−∞,3]; the second has range(−∞,1).
steps: For a<1 there are 2 roots; for 1≤a≤3 only the first branch contributes; for a>3 there are none.
Two valid choices are a=1 (root −3) and a=3 (root 1).
problems.answer: For example, a=1 and a=3. All such a lie in[1,3].

problems.title: Angles from three arcs
problems.question: A triangle’s vertices divide its circumcircle into arcs in ratio3:4:5. Find the angles.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: The arcs sum 360°, so they are 90°,120°,150°. An inscribed angle is half its opposite arc.

problems.title: Externally tangent circles in a60° angle
problems.question: Two circles touch externally, and their two common external tangent rays meet at 60°. The smaller diameter is 10. Find the larger radius.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: Let radii be r=5, R. The centres lie on the angle bisector, at distances r/sin30° and R/sin30° from the tangent intersection.
steps: Their distance is 2(R−r), and external tangency also makes it R+r. Thus 2R−2r=R+r, so R=3r=15.
problems.note: The 60° angle is interpreted as the angle between tangent rays pointing toward the circles, the usual convention for this configuration.

problems.title: Equal chords and a diameter
problems.question: EC=CD,∠ECD=54°, and BD is a diameter, with points in the pictured order. Find∠BDC.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: Triangle ECD is isosceles, so∠CED=(180−54)/2=63°. Angles CBD and CED subtend the same chord CD, so∠CBD=63°.

problems.title: An arc-midpoint chord question
problems.question: C is midpoint of minor arc AB. Chords CD, CK meet AB at M, N. Given∠AMC=140°, find∠DKC.
problems.idea: Use a graph, an equation, or a circle-angle relation to turn the data into a direct calculation.
formulas: Put arc AC=arc CB=t. The intersecting-chord theorem gives arc AC+arc BD=280°. Hence the other arc from C to D through A has measure80°.
steps: If K is outside that80° arc, the inscribed angle DKC is 40°. If K lies on that arc, the intercepted arc is 280° and the angle is 140°.
The stated conditions do not specify the order of M, N or exclude either K position.
problems.note: A unique40° answer requires K to lie outside the minor CD arc. The printed question supplies no diagram or ordering condition selecting this case.
